sections.h2: Where is the Greene County Register of Deeds, and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office is in the Greene County Courthouse at 301 N. Greene Street in Snow Hill, NC 28580, and it is open 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Monday through Friday, excluding holidays. The phone number is 252-747-3620, and the mailing address is PO Box 86, Snow Hill, NC 28580.

The office calls itself the custodian of the county's real estate documents and vital records. It files and records deeds, deeds of trust, maps, easements, leases, assignments and Uniform Commercial Code filings that act as fixture filings on real property. Notary commissions are recorded there too, and the office swears in notaries who live in the county.

The county's tax rate page lists three towns, Hookerton, Snow Hill and Walstonburg. A deed for land in any of them is recorded at this one courthouse office.

sections.h2: What must go with a deed recorded in Greene County?
sections.html:
Every deed to be recorded in Greene County must come with a tax form signed by the Greene County Tax Office. The register of deeds' page says the Deed Information form is needed before any deed is recorded.

The county's form asks for these items:

  • Grantor and grantee names and addresses.
  • The address and legal description of the property being transferred, plus any buildings or improvements if the deed is a split.
  • Personal property that conveys with the land, with a mobile home given as the example.
  • Whether deferred tax value is involved, and the family relationship between grantor and grantee if so.
  • Prior-year taxes and current-year tax due, which the tax office fills in.

The tax office also assigns the parcel identification number and marks whether the deed is a transfer, a split or a merge. A line for the office's approval, signed and dated, sits at the bottom. The form's notes say deeds with delinquent taxes follow separate instructions on the reverse, so ask the tax office at 252-747-3615 how any back taxes on your parcel must be handled before you go to the courthouse.

sections.h2: How does e-recording work in Greene County?
sections.html:
The Greene County Register of Deeds accepts e-recordings of everything except maps and highway rights-of-way. A lawyer or settlement agent can therefore file a deed without a trip to Snow Hill.

The tax form changes for electronic filers. The county form says the tax office can approve Deed Information sheets only through the electronic recording platform, and that filers should not send anything directly to the tax office. That is the part first-time e-filers miss, since a paper packet and an electronic packet take different routes to the same approval.

Online searching is available from 1875 to the present on the county's land records site, run by Courthouse Computer Systems. The county moved its register of deeds to that system in December 2025, and the office can answer questions about it at 252-747-3620.

sections.h2: How much does the state charge to record a deed in Greene County?
sections.html:
Recording fees are set by G.S. 161-10 and are the same in all North Carolina counties. For a general instrument the fee is $26.00 for the first 15 pages plus $4.00 per additional page, and for a deed of trust or mortgage it is $64.00 for the first 35 pages plus $4.00 per additional page.

  • Satisfactions and cancellations of deeds of trust or mortgages: no fee.
  • Plats: $21.00 per sheet.
  • Certified copies: $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each additional page.
  • Nonstandard documents: a $25.00 add-on.
  • Extra instruments in one document: $10.00 each.

The statute calls the schedule complete and exclusive, with fees collected before filing. Other charges at the Greene counter are unrelated to deeds: the county page prices a certified birth, death or marriage copy at $10.00 in cash and a marriage license at $60, cash only.

sections.h2: Who pays the transfer tax on a Greene County deed?
sections.html:
The seller pays it. G.S. 105-228.30 puts an excise tax on each instrument conveying an interest in real property at $1.00 for each $500 of consideration or value, counting any fraction of $500, and the transferor pays the register of deeds before recording.

Half of the collection goes to the county general fund. The other half, less refunds and an allowance, is sent each month to the Department of Revenue, with a 2% allowance for the county on the state share. A parcel that crosses a county line is taxed in the county with the greater value.

Because the tax follows the consideration stated in the deed, check the number against the contract before the deed is sent for recording. Under G.S. 47-18 a deed binds later buyers and lien creditors only from the time it is registered, so a submission rejected for a missing tax form or a wrong amount leaves a gap.

sections.h2: What are the Greene County property tax rates and listing rules?
sections.html:
The Greene County Tax Department posts a county rate of $0.7835 per $100 on its 2026 rates page, and towns and fire districts add to it. The tax office is at 229 Kingold Boulevard, Suite B, Snow Hill, with PO Box 482 and phone 252-747-3615, open 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays.

Greene County 2026 rates as the county Tax Rates page prints them (https://greenecountync.gov/departments/tax/tax-rates/)

The same page lists eleven fire districts, from Arba at $0.0700 to Fort Run at $0.1220, plus a Middle Swamp service district at $0.0910. Personal property such as mobile homes, boats, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles must be listed from January 1 through January 31, and a late listing carries a ten percent penalty.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Greene County?
sections.html:
Greene County had 20,700 residents on July 1, 2025, up 1.2% from the 2020 estimates base, on about 267 square miles of land. That works out to about 77 people per square mile.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 66.5% for 2020 to 2024.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $117,400.
  • Median gross rent: $853.
  • Median household income: $53,244.
  • Persons in poverty: 19.9%.
  • Housing units: 8,070 as of July 1, 2025.

Median home value here sits well below the $247,700 shown for Granville County and the $244,800 shown for Greensboro on the same Census table, so the fixed recording fees and the excise tax of $1.00 per $500 take a different share of a sale than they would in a county with higher values. The Census counts 59 building permits for 2025. Use these as county-wide medians, not as a price for one house.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Greene County, NC?
faqs.a: At the Register of Deeds in the courthouse at 301 N. Greene Street, Snow Hill, open 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays except holidays. E-recording is accepted for everything except maps and highway rights-of-way.

faqs.q: Do I need the tax office to sign off on a Greene County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. The register of deeds' page says every deed must be accompanied by a tax form signed by the Greene County Tax Office, and the county's Deed Information form is the one to use. For e-recordings the approval happens through the electronic platform.

faqs.q: How much is the excise tax on a Greene County deed?
faqs.a: It is $1.00 on each $500 of the consideration or value, counting a fraction of $500 as a full unit, under G.S. 105-228.30. The seller pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What phone number reaches the Greene County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 252-747-3620. The tax office is a separate line, 252-747-3615, and its hours are 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays.

faqs.q: How far back do Greene County online deed searches go?
faqs.a: The register of deeds' page says online index searches run from 1875 through the present. The office moved to a new records system in December 2025.
